title: Sliding-window batcher + KV-bank compaction for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Mixed workloads with long prompts and long expected responses create two pressure sources: (1) batcher slot fragmentation when short-response requests are interleaved with long-response requests; (2) KV cache memory churn when many long-prefix dialogues touch large KV allocations. Current continuous-batching scheduler occasionally either (a) prioritizes latency for short dialogs but underutilizes GPU throughput for long completions, or (b) packs aggressively and causes OOMs or excessive KV eviction during tails.

Goal: Implement and validate a sliding-window batcher paired with a KV-bank compaction policy to improve overall throughput and reduce peak GPU memory usage while keeping short-dialog p95 latency within SLA. The sliding-window batcher should allow controlled coalescing of adjacent slots with similar lifetime expectations. The KV-bank compaction will group KV allocations into "banks" by session length profile and age, performing opportunistic compaction and eviction under memory-watermark signals.

Scope: scheduler and runtime changes only (no API/SDK changes). Includes simulation harness, microbenchmarks, and 2-stage rollout (canary in staging cluster then gradual production rollout).
acceptance_criteria: Throughput: end-to-end token/sec increases by >= 8% on the mixed-50/50 long-short dataset compared to baseline continuous-batcher
Memory: 99th percentile GPU memory usage per worker reduced by >= 18% under peak synthetic load
Latency: short-dialog p95 latency degradation <= 10% relative to baseline (absolute p95 must remain <= 220ms on 8xA100 node)
Stability: no OOMs in 24h soak at target QPS during canary
Observability: added metrics and dashboards for bank hit-rate, compaction cycles, slot-coalesce events, and memory-watermark transitions
Feature flags: implementation behind runtime config flag and rolloutable via canary target group
experiment_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation: extend existing workload simulator to model mixed prompt/response length distributions and KV lifetime; run 72h stress runs to validate heuristics
Phase 1 - Staging Canary: deploy with feature flag to staging pool (10% of capacity) and run synthetic and sampled production traces for 48h
Phase 2 - Gradual Production Rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% by capacity with monitoring gates at each step (throughput, p95, GPU memory)
A/B comparisons: baseline continuous-batcher vs sliding-window+kv-bank (collect token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, OOMs, evictions)
Rollback plan: automatic rollback on memory OOMs or latency SLO breaches exceeding thresholds for >5 minutes
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated behind runtime config 'sliding_window_batcher_v1'
Canary: enable on dedicated staging pool for 12 hours with synthetic trace, then 48 hours with sampled traffic
Production: ramp to 25% capacity and hold 2 hours; if all gates pass, ramp to 50% for 4 hours; then 100%
Monitoring: automated alert if gpu_memory_used_p99 > baseline*0.95 or short_dialog_p95 > 1.1*baseline
Post-rollout: 7-day golden metrics review and follow-up tuning ticket if bank hit_rate < 70%

2026-01-14 Ethan Zhao: Prototype sliding-window coalescing added to simulator. Initial microbench shows 5% throughput improvement but memory reduction negligible; hypothesis: KV grouping heuristic too coarse.
